options: Merging datasets into a single presentation view
Deleting duplicate records from a warehouse
Connecting with one or more source systems to pull data
Building a dashboard for business users
Encrypting data in transit between systems
questions.explanation: Data Integration is to connect with one or more source systems to pull data; it is the prerequisite for blending.

options: Merging all datasets into one viewable and understandable presentation view to answer business KPIs
Pulling data from a single source system
Storing raw data in a Data Lake
Removing special characters from text fields
Assigning access rights to tables
questions.explanation: Data Blending merges all datasets into one viewable and understandable presentation view in order to answer business KPIs.

questions.stem: How are Data Integration and Data Blending related?
options: Data Blending is the prerequisite for Data Integration
They are two names for the same process
Data Blending replaces Data Integration in a Data Lake
Data Integration is the prerequisite process for Data Blending
They are performed by different departments and never interact
questions.explanation: Data Integration is the prerequisite for Data Blending: if you cannot get data from source systems, you cannot blend it to present to management.

questions.stem: What single goal do Data Science, Business Intelligence and every kind of Analytics all work towards, according to I Am Datapedia!?
options: Reducing storage costs
Achieving one or another business KPI
Replacing the IT department
Building the largest possible Data Lake
Automating data entry
questions.explanation: The author's 'one big fat reality' is that all of these disciplines work toward achieving one or the other business KPI.

questions.stem: In the product-sales example, a product is sold from a shop, an online website and a mobile application. Why is this a blending challenge?
options: Because the product has a different price in each channel
Because only the shop stores its data in a database
Because the website has no transaction data
Because a Data Warehouse cannot hold more than one channel
Because the different systems may store transactions in different ways, yet all must be gathered into one target table
questions.explanation: Loading product transactions from all systems into one target table is not simple because different systems may store transactions in different patterns.

questions.stem: What does the development team create during the Blending process?
options: Joins, unions and other transformation logic to convert all transaction types into one standardised list
New source systems for each sales channel
A separate warehouse for every channel
Access policies for business users
A backup of every source table
questions.explanation: In the Blending process the development team creates joins, unions and all kinds of transformation logic to blend the different product-selling transactions into one standardised list.

questions.stem: In a nutshell, what does the Blending process assist with?
options: Compressing historical data
Presenting standardised data in dashboards and reports for business users' decision making
Granting authentication to new employees
Pulling raw data from source systems
Choosing a NoSQL database
questions.explanation: In a nutshell, blending assists in presenting standardised data in dashboards and reporting so business users can make decisions.

questions.stem: Which sources of data are mentioned as possible inputs to blending in the current era?
options: Only relational databases
Only spreadsheets and CSV files
Social media, videos, audios, PDFs and emails
Only data warehouses
Only mobile applications
questions.explanation: In this era data can come from social media, videos, audios, PDFs, emails and more.

questions.stem: What has made it possible to blend structured, semi-structured and unstructured data into one comprehensive view?
options: The retirement of Data Warehouses
The use of a single sales channel
The end of social media data
The introduction of Data Lakes
The five-KPI dashboard rule
questions.explanation: With the introduction of Data Lakes, all kinds of data, structured, semi-structured or unstructured, can be blended into one comprehensive view to target a business KPI.

questions.stem: Which statement about Data Integration and Data Blending is NOT correct?
options: They are core to the Data Pipeline
They are commonly confused with each other
In the product example the target system is a Data Warehouse
Blending produces a standardised list of transactions
Blending can be done without first integrating data from source systems
questions.explanation: Blending depends on integration: if you cannot get data from the source systems, you cannot blend it.
